findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the fan-in selection rule in child 761e's plan text: replace 'exec: LLM' with the actual predicate (`exec` ∈ {1-TURN, 2-STEP, AGENT}, equivalently `exec != DET`) and co-locate it alongside the exec vocabulary definition at `overlay.py` or in the docs/llm-framework.md runtime contract section.
evidence: Child 761e plan text: 'Select active project. ids whose routing entry has exec: LLM; DET-tier project criteria remain outside this LLM finder path.'
overlay.py:154 defines the valid exec vocabulary as: '1-TURN', '2-STEP', 'AGENT', 'DET' — 'LLM' is not listed.
gate_dispatch.py:631: `str((routing.get(criterion_id) or {}).get('exec', '1-TURN')).upper() != 'DET'` — the actual filter is negation-of-DET, not equality-to-LLM.
The plan never defines 'LLM' as an exec vocabulary alias, and no mapping from 'LLM' → {1-TURN, 2-STEP, AGENT} is documented alongside the fan-in decision rule.
findings.finding: Child ticket 761e's plan text specifies 'Select active project. ids whose routing entry has exec: LLM' as the decision rule for fan-in admission, but 'LLM' is not a member of the defined exec vocabulary (1-TURN, 2-STEP, AGENT, DET at overlay.py:154). The actual implemented filter is `!= "DET"` (gate_dispatch.py:631), which admits 1-TURN/2-STEP/AGENT — a different rule that is not stated in the plan. A future implementer reading the plan would apply exec == 'LLM' filtering, which would match nothing and silently exclude all project criteria from Round A.
findings.location: Delivered decomposition / child fc72 fan-in approach section; src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:631; src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:154
scenarios: A future author writing a new code-review project criterion follows the plan's 'exec: LLM' wording and sets that value in their routing entry — overlay validation rejects it as an unknown exec value.

A future implementer reading the plan to add a second gate's fan-in step implements exec == 'LLM' filtering, which silently excludes all project criteria whose entries use the real vocab values (1-TURN/AGENT).
findings.suggested_fix: In the runtime contract documentation (docs/llm-framework.md) and child 761e's plan text, replace 'exec: LLM' with: 'Select active project. ids whose routing entry has exec ≠ DET (i.e., exec ∈ {1-TURN, 2-STEP, AGENT}); DET-tier project criteria remain outside the LLM finder path.' Cross-reference this against the valid exec vocabulary defined in overlay.py.

findings.finding: Child 9447 declares a hard dependency on external ticket `3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5` ('landed repository-root seam repair') — a ticket that is neither one of the eight epic children nor mentioned anywhere in the parent plan — creating an untracked external precondition that could block parent AC7 with no mitigation path in the epic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback / back-out plan (e.g., overlay-disable flag, revert commit procedure, or feature-flag) for the live Gerrit deployment and production-file seam changes, and reference it in AC-7 and the epic description.
evidence: 'advisory live-Gerrit dogfood, including the repaired repository-root seam and the cleaned final prompt revision' — live deployment with no stated rollback
'The no-overlay runtime preserves the ordered 13 built-ins' — only a test assertion, not a back-out procedure
No 'rollback', 'revert', 'back-out', 'canary', or 'feature flag' language anywhere in the plan
AC-7 requires operator attestation that the change is merged, but no condition under which to revert
findings.finding: The plan modifies multiple live production files (criterion-id resolver, batch runner, gate dispatch, workflow ops, eval solver, CLI) and deploys to a live Gerrit bot (child `9447`), but provides no explicit rollback or back-out plan for any of these changes. AC-3's parity test is a regression *guard*, not a reversibility mechanism; if the live deployment breaks the Gerrit bot, there is no stated procedure to revert.
findings.location: AC-7 (child `9447` live Gerrit deployment); AC-3 (no-overlay parity); Delivered decomposition (all eight production-file seam children)
scenarios: The criterion-id resolver change in `ids.py` introduces a regression in packaged-criteria resolution not caught by the parity test; the deployed Gerrit bot begins dropping reviews with no documented recovery path.
The live Gerrit change merged under child `9447` causes unexpected LLM routing behavior in production; there is no stated procedure to disable or revert the project-criteria overlay.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-paragraph 'Rollback' section to the epic: (1) the project-criteria overlay can be disabled by removing/emptying the repository overlay config, restoring packaged-only behavior; (2) child `9447`'s Gerrit change can be reverted via a named revert commit; (3) define the operator signal (e.g., `coverage.llm_ran: false` or error rate threshold) that triggers the rollback.

scenarios: Threshold needs tightening after observing false-positive rates in production Gerrit reviews

findings.suggested_fix: Add a config entry (e.g. in the repository overlay schema) such as `code_review.project_criteria.routing_threshold: 0.90` and `code_review.project_criteria.blocking: false`; reference that key from child `9447`'s implementation and note it in `docs/llm-framework.md`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief positive rationale to the epic plan (e.g., in the Context/Problem or Delivered decomposition section) explaining why the eight-child disjoint-file-set decomposition was chosen over alternatives such as a single consolidated refactor or a capability flag — e.g., it isolates blast radius, enables independent plan-review/completion-verification per seam, and preserves backward compatibility at each step.
evidence: The plan says 'The eight child tickets are dependency-ordered and closed' and lists the file-impact sets, but provides no rationale for why eight disjoint children (rather than, e.g., a single PR or a capability flag) was the right design for this epic.
Each individual child ticket does provide local approach rationale, but the epic plan itself — the document under review — contains no summary statement of why this decomposition strategy was chosen.
G6 criterion 4: 'The plan states a POSITIVE rationale for the chosen approach (its absence is a finding)'
findings.finding: The epic plan does not state a positive rationale for its chosen overall decomposition approach — specifically, why eight dependency-ordered children with disjoint file-impact sets was chosen over alternatives such as a single consolidated refactor or a feature-flag rollout. The plan describes the structure and what was done, but not why this approach was selected as the best fit for this codebase and team context.
scenarios: A reviewer reading only the epic plan cannot determine whether the disjoint-file decomposition was chosen for safety reasons, parallel development, atomic rollback, CI blast-radius, or another purpose.
An implementer picking up a follow-on epic cannot use this plan as a template without understanding why this structure was selected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 1–3 sentences to the 'Delivered decomposition' section, e.g.: 'This seam-by-seam decomposition was chosen because each drop point is owned by a distinct production module; disjoint file sets allow independent plan-review, completion-verification, and rollback at each seam without risk of one change destabilizing another. A single consolidated refactor would have made it impossible to isolate the root cause if any seam misbehaved in live Gerrit reviews.'
